# isNumberLike

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is convertible to a number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isNumberLike() — Checks whether a value is convertible to a number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isNumberLike(value: unknown): boolean;
```

A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is convertible to a number; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isNumberLike(1); // => true
isNumberLike("1.5"); // => true
isNumberLike(" 42 "); // => true
isNumberLike(NaN); // => false
isNumberLike(Infinity); // => false
isNumberLike(""); // => false
isNumberLike(null); // => false
```
